speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether he can provide an update on the progress of the 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) since their announcement in 2016; (b) whether the objectives set out for each of the clusters/industries have been achieved; and (c) whether the Government is planning for ITM 2.0 and, if so, when will it be rolled out given the current economic downturn and disruption.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what is the progress of the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs); (b) whether the Ministry plans to make changes to the ITMs in view of the impact of COVID-19 on the economy; (c) whether the impact of workplace transformation has been considered in each of the 23 ITMs; and (d) whether the ITMs can specifically address the upskilling, re-training and hiring of mature workers, workers with disabilities and other vulnerable groups of workers for an inclusive transformation of the industries.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have seen encouraging progress since embarking on our Industry Transformation Map (ITM) journey in 2016.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Up to 2019, our ITMs have been progressing well, with most of them on track to meet their targets.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some of our ITM sectors, such as Air Transport, Hotels and Retail were badly hit, and will take time to recover.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is why as part of the series of Budget measures, we provided special support for the harder hit sectors, to help them stay resilient.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We target to complete this by next year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our ITM refresh is complemented by the work of the Emerging Stronger Taskforce and the Singapore Together Alliances for Action, which have served as pathfinders to help us seize immediate opportunities, even amidst COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ultimately, we transform our economy for the benefit of our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our ITMs chart the path forward for each sector to be competitive, so that our people can access good jobs and opportunities which improve their lives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Jobs and Skills are therefore key pillars of each ITM, supported through initiatives such as the next bound of SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We pay specific attention to mid-career workers, to help them stay employable and access good jobs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our tripartite partners have also been working closely together to ensure that business transformation is tied to workplace and workforce transformation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For example, Workforce Singapore has worked with Government agencies and industry to develop Jobs Transformation Maps to provide detailed insights on the impact of technology and innovation on the industry and workforce.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Labour Movement has also been working with businesses to establish Company Training Committees, to help our workers upgrade while supporting their companies' transformation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: More immediately, the Labour Movement's Job Security Council is working hard to match and place workers, minimise retrenchments and shorten unemployment periods for our workers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This way, we achieve inclusive growth which uplifts our workers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government is acutely aware of the plight of vulnerable workers who have been hardest hit by the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have, therefore, been providing additional support for these workers who require more time and effort to reskill, upskill and re-join the workforce.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A higher level of support is provided to employers who hire mature local workers, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help our senior workers, the Senior Employment Credit provides wage offsets for businesses that employ Singaporean workers aged 55 and above.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have also introduced the Enabling Employment Credit, which provides employers with wage offsets for every Singaporean person with disabilities earning below $4,000 per month that they employ.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will continue to build on these schemes to ensure that no one is left behind as we work with our tripartite partners to emerge stronger from the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I hope, as MTI and the respective sectoral ITMs flesh out their updates and do their revisions, to share where the jobs growth opportunities are as we overcome and emerge stronger together post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The second supplementary question I have is with respect to the ITMs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I hope to see more best sharing of good practices and the successes and the key success factors as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: But I also want to urge MTI as we look at the 23 ITMs and as we prepare for the next bound, to continue the good work of the sectoral tripartite committees because I felt, being personally involved in some of them, they are very useful in overcoming the sectoral challenges.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: So, I urge that, as we prepare for the next bound, to continue the good work of these sectoral tripartite committees.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To his first question on looking for new growth opportunities, I fully agree with him.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In fact, as I have mentioned in my reply earlier, a post-COVID-19 world will be a very different world.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are already seeing many of these changes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Changes have been accelerated and, in particular, technological trends have also been accelerated, especially digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As I have said in my Budget speeches before, COVID-19 has accelerated digitalisation in a way which very few CTOs have been able to do.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There have been significant changes in the nature of work and even in the nature of the way businesses conduct themselves.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I must say that our agencies are already responding to that quite well.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some of our MNCs and large local enterprises are on par with our global peers in this digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What this digitalisation trend means is that the nature of the job and the nature of skills will be very different, which is why it is critical that we develop those skills of our workers in this respect.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are another part which is about the Attachments programme so that workers can get attached to get a sense of the nature of the job and companies can have a chance to evaluate the workers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For workers in newer areas, they can also go for training.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These are the different ways in which we are preparing our workers and to grow our Singaporean Core, to move Singaporeans into areas with growth opportunities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On Mr Patrick Tay's second question about the varying success of the ITMs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In fact, whether you do ITM or you do not do ITM, the nature of economic growth cannot be predicted in advance.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You cannot say that in five years, these sectors will grow; in five years, these sectors will shrink.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There are sectors which will face more challenging conditions for which we are helping them to stay resilient.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I mentioned that air transport and tourism are the most obvious areas from this COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But at the same time, even in normal times, you will find that some sectors will grow faster than others.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Therefore, the way that we are helping our workers is to ensure that we provide as much training as possible – and that is where I want to commend our Labour Movement for the very good work that they are doing – both in starting the company training committee so that when companies are looking at how they will change and transform, at the same time, the union is working together with them to look at how the workers can be retrained for that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And this is not something to be taken for granted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I think this tripartism where our Labour Movement is not there to just oppose change but, in fact, to facilitate change so that, at the end of the day, whatever changes that are made can be sustainable in that you have the full support of our workers and our workers can have a better life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, this is really the crux of this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I want to thank Mr Patrick Tay and his team for their very hard work in the Labour Movement in doing this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked whether there would be sharing of good practices.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On Mr Patrick Tay's point on the sectoral tripartite committee, I fully agree with him.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These are important work in which we bring all our stakeholders together so that we put our efforts together to achieve a greater impact.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I would like to thank Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Sharael Taha for their questions.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that the ITMs began a few years ago, much has changed since then and we have learnt a lot in the past one year from the pandemic and changing macroeconomic situation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Are we incorporating these lessons learnt and revising the ITMs to better prepare ourselves for the future?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For example, in the manufacturing ITM, should we be incorporating capability for vaccination production or preparing for PPE production in preparation for the next pandemic?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And for the healthcare ITM, should we explore the use of technology or develop more skills to build latent capacity in our healthcare system that can be called upon and scaled up quickly when the next pandemic arises?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For the second question, coincidentally, today marks the first day, after close to a year, where working from home is no longer the default work arrangement.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In an earlier Straits Times poll, three in four respondents do not wish to return to the workplace full-time.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Work from home or work from anywhere has brought about many benefits for both businesses and employees, including for the vulnerable workers and workers with mobility challenges.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Not only does it allow jobs to be more accessible to all, it could also be a competitive advantage for companies in Singapore to vie for jobs outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This could be a game-changer for our professional services ITM.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we lock in the gains of remote and flexi-work arrangements before we revert back to the pre-COVID norms?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we relook at the opportunities to incorporate this into our ITM, moving forward?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, not only can we work from home, we can work from anywhere and you get calls any time as well.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the Member's question about the skills, for example, healthcare and for us to move towards digitalisation, indeed, that should be the way.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And as I have said, digitalisation has been accelerated and we must take this opportunity to look at how we can not only digitalise as much of our companies' processes as possible but also help our workers to build the new skills to be able to access those opportunities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And, in fact, beyond that, I have seen in many of our community centres, for example, that many seniors are being taught how to use digital tools – and I just did one over the weekend – as well as the projects to help our hawkers go digital, help our stallholders go digital and these are achieving good progress.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I will say, certainly, we must take into account the changes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If you can work from home, anybody in the world can also work from home.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I have seen, for example, videos of how workers in very, very depressed areas being able to access jobs in very advanced economies because all they needed was a knowledge of English, a knowledge of basic skills in doing what they were good at doing, a laptop and an Internet connection.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I have seen companies that have actually chopped up a very complex project into different bits and different parts for which they put it online for bidding and then you have workers all over the world bidding for those projects.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And in one of the reports I saw, the worker was extremely happy because he had never earned that amount in his whole life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The company was extremely happy because the the cost to him was a fraction of what he had to pay in an advanced economy with very strong laws regarding employment and so on.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, it is a major, major opportunity but also a major challenge.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That is why in all of last year's Budgets and this year's Budget, we have placed a very, very strong emphasis on upgrading the skills of our workers and I look forward to our Labour Movement working closely together with us on the Company Training Committee and a Job Security Council so that we can help our workers access good jobs, better jobs and to be able to ride on this digitalisation trend.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I hope that the work that we are going to embark on in a refreshed way, linking our R&D efforts with the economic sectors and pulling together these different strengths of efforts will enable us to make even better progress.
